source_text:
3.19 Ἀφρικανοῦ Τοὺς σκώληκας κλύσμασιν ἀφαρμάκτοις
ἐκβαλεῖν ὕδωρ ἐμοὶ καθαρὸν ἀρκεῖ ληφθὲν τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον· ἀντίχειρι καὶ τῷ
ἰατρικῷ δακτύλῳ χειρὸς εὐωνύμου ἀρυσάμενος ἐπεστραμμένως «ἀθολώτου νάματι
πηγῆς» τὸν νοσοῦντα τοὺς σκώληκας τόπον τρὶς ῥᾶνον. Οἱ δὲ ἐξελεύσονται πάντες
ἐφέποντες ἀλλήλοις, καταλειπομένου ἔνδον οὐδενός. 3. Ἀφρικανοῦ Ὅτι ὄνος
ἁπάντων τῶν ζῴων οὔτε φθεῖρας οὔτε κρότωνας φέρει.
pass_a_gloss: 3.19 Of-Africanus. The worms with-clysters unmedicated to-cast-out water to-me clean suffices having-been-taken the manner this: with-thumb and the medical finger of-hand left having-drawn turned-back 'of-unmuddied stream of-a-spring' the being-sick the worms place thrice sprinkle. They but will-come-out all following one-another, being-left-behind inside of-nothing. 3. Of-Africanus That a-donkey of-all the animals neither lice nor ticks bears.
pass_b_english: Of Africanus. To cast out the worms with unmedicated clysters, clean water is enough for me, taken in this manner: having drawn with the thumb and the medical finger of the left hand, turned back, sprinkle the place sick with the worms three times with “unmuddied stream of a spring.” They will all come out following one another, nothing being left behind inside.
Of Africanus. That a donkey, of all the animals, bears neither lice nor ticks.

choices.why: Kept as the lock's quoted formula, not flattened to 'clean water' which the prose already has.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
